output.title: Where churn signals actually begin
output.body:
Churn signals usually do not begin in a dashboard. They begin when an owner notices that the same customers are going quiet, buying less often, or asking for help in a different tone than before.

For a 1–10 person business, the useful workflow decision is not “should we use AI?” It is: do we have a repeatable way to spot the patterns that appear before a customer stops repeating, or is this still just a vague monthly worry? AI only helps once the pattern is already visible in your records.

So the first practical step is simple: review one month of cancellations or lapses and list the last visible touchpoints, complaints, delays, or periods of silence beforehand. Check email, CRM notes, order history, and support messages. If those signals show up in the same places more than once, you have a bounded pilot. If they do not, the work stays manual a bit longer. Annoying, but honest.

That keeps the decision where it should be: with the owner, using the records already on hand, before any automation enters the picture.
